reasons.text: Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 308% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 100% of months
Electricity bought is only 0.18x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (27 kWh/t against at least 150)
85% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Sold products equal only 17% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
74% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)

inspection_checklist: Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
